description: Fix concrete performance, UX, and accessibility issues in the interactive components, without introducing risky architectural changes (branch must stay working; syncs to Lovable). Three targeted problems: (1) the hero video keeps decoding a looping video while scrolled off-screen; (2) the PinnedServicesShowcase is effectively hover-driven with poor touch discoverability and its stacked preview images all expose real alt text so screen readers announce four overlapping descriptions for one visible image; (3) confirm the multiple simultaneous scroll listeners are each reduced-motion guarded and rAF-gated (they are) and make no regressions. All changes must preserve prefers-reduced-motion behaviour.
steps: src/components/hero-video.tsx: pause the <video> when it scrolls out of view and resume when it returns (respecting the existing reduced-motion + playing state logic and the manual pause toggle). Use an IntersectionObserver on the video/container: when not intersecting, call video.pause(); when intersecting again and reduced-motion is not set and the user has not manually paused, resume play(). Do not fight the existing user-facing play/pause button — track whether the pause was user-initiated vs visibility-initiated so the manual state is respected. Clean up the observer in the effect's return. Keep the existing scroll-tilt rAF logic.

src/components/pinned-services-showcase.tsx: improve touch/keyboard discoverability and fix a11y. (a) The four stacked preview in .cinema-services-visual-wrap are decorative duplicates layered by opacity; give the non-active images empty alt (alt="") and aria-hidden, or render alt only for the active image, so assistive tech announces one image, not four. (b) Each row is role="button" with tabIndex=0 and Enter/Space handlers — verify keyboard activation works and add a visible focus style hook if none exists (coordinate with styles.css: the .cinema-service-item has hover/is-active styles at ~line 2806; ensure :focus-visible gets the same active treatment so keyboard users see the reveal). (c) Consider making the reveal also respond to focus (onFocus setActiveIdx) so keyboard tab-through reveals each service body, matching the hover behaviour.

In src/styles.css, add a :focus-visible rule for .cinema-service-item that mirrors the .is-active / hover visual treatment (background + title color) so keyboard focus is clearly visible. Match the existing OKLCH color-mix pattern used at .cinema-service-item.is-active (~line 2817). Do not restructure unrelated CSS.

Review (do not necessarily change) the set of scroll listeners across scroll-focus-stack.tsx, content-sections.tsx (ServicesGrid), scroll-progress.tsx, projects-showcase-grid.tsx, and site-shell.tsx: confirm each is passive, rAF-gated, and reduced-motion guarded. If any listener is found NOT reduced-motion guarded or NOT cleaned up on unmount, fix it. Record findings; do not merge them into a shared controller (too risky for this branch).
acceptance_criteria: hero-video.tsx pauses the video when off-screen and resumes when back on-screen, respects prefers-reduced-motion, respects a user-initiated pause (does not auto-resume something the user paused), and disconnects its IntersectionObserver on cleanup.
In pinned-services-showcase.tsx, only one image description is exposed to assistive tech at a time (inactive stacked images have alt="" and/or aria-hidden).
.cinema-service-item has a visible :focus-visible state in styles.css matching its active treatment, and keyboard focus reveals the active service (via onFocus or existing key handling).
All scroll listeners remain passive, rAF-gated, reduced-motion guarded, and cleaned up on unmount; any that were not are fixed.
Edits match existing Prettier/ESLint formatting so lint stays clean.
verification: Read hero-video.tsx and confirm an IntersectionObserver pauses/resumes with reduced-motion and manual-pause guards plus cleanup
Read pinned-services-showcase.tsx and confirm inactive images are hidden from a11y and focus reveals the service
In CI: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm test, npm run build all pass
